data.narrative:
Mariana Minerals is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Turner Caldwell that has raised $95M to date. The valuation peer set comprises one public company (LNZA) and eight private firms in the climate and energy sector, including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

A Stage-Progression method was the only applicable triangulation approach, given insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables to support a reliable Peer-Median analysis. The Climate & Energy sector contains eight known peers, but none met the minimum threshold of three datapoints within the narrow stage or valuation-tier filters required for median-based valuation. The Stage-Progression method applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage progression to the $95M raised baseline, implying a valuation of $190M.

The triangulated range anchors to $190M as the median point, with a low of $162M (reflecting downside risk) and a high of $218M (reflecting upside scenarios under favorable capital-market conditions). This single-method result carries material uncertainty given the absence of a robust private peer median for the sector. Key sensitivities include macro conditions affecting climate-tech funding velocity, the composition and liquidity horizons of the existing $95M capital base, and the target's stage-specific milestones relative to peer cohorts in Materials, Energy Storage, and Critical Minerals.
